messages:
sara.ops: FYI a customer on Dedicated reported large throughput drop and intermittent 429s for the last ~45m. They saw latency jump and token/sec falloff. posting customer timeline + sample API error: 

miguel.eng: Can you paste the exact error they see? 429s usually mean throttle, but on Dedicated we should see graceful backpressure, not repeated client errors.

sara.ops: here's the sample: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-err: RateLimitExceeded
timestamp: 2025-11-03T17:12:08Z
body: {"message":"request rejected: unable to pack into batch within SLO"}
```

alex-oncall: interesting message: "unable to pack into batch within SLO" -> that's our continuous batcher failing to build a viable pack before timeout. Could be tiny max_batch_tokens or aggressive pack_timeout. Any recent config changes on that pool?

miguel.eng: Checking infra dashboard... Dedicated pool "dp-west-42" saw sustained queue length of 60, but packing rate dropped and avg batch tokens is ~12 while model max tokens is 2048. CPU of sequencer pod spiking. I can share a grafana snapshot.

sara.ops: customer said they ramped 2x qps yesterday for a migration, then saw throughput collapse. They didn't change model or prompt size.

julie-se: Hypothesis: micro-batches due to token-ceiling config + fairqueue mis-prioritizing tenants. If most requests are short, packer might prefer high-priority tenant leading to starvation for medium ones -> oscillation.

miguel.eng: I'm seeing many tiny batches (1-3 requests) and a sharp increase in prefill attempts per request. The packer log shows repeated prefill retries and a lot of dropped attempts: 
```
[packer] packed 2 reqs (tot_tokens=18) in 5ms
[packer] attempt timeout after 120ms (min_pack_tokens=64)
[packer] prefill retry: seq=...
```

alex-oncall: That "min_pack_tokens=64" is odd given avg_tot_tokens=12. If min_pack_tokens > typical bundle size, packer will wait until SLO and then timeout, producing 429/backpressure and tiny fallback paths. Did someone change default pack thresholds?

miguel.eng: I checked the last deploy: config commit 2025-11-03 15:00 by infra-bot bumped continuous.batch.min_batch_tokens from 8 -> 64 to reduce small batches for other tenants. That explains it. It improved econ for high-QPS customers but killed this customer's workload when they spiked short requests.

sara.ops: Customer is on a Dedicated pool shared with 3 mid-size tenants. They expected isolation. They escalated to enterprise support asking for a rollback or mitigation.

julie-se: Mitigations (fast): 1) temporarily lower min_batch_tokens back to 8 for dp-west-42 via runtime patch; 2) add a tenant-based packing override so short-request tenant gets lower min threshold; 3) scale pool up to increase pack search velocity.

alex-oncall: For short term I can flip config flag on that pool to 8 in the next 5m. But we should confirm no regression for other tenants. Any A/B guardrails?

miguel.eng: We can target just that DP with a config roll (runtime supports per-dp flags). I'll run a canary on 1 node, watch pack success rate and token/sec.

sara.ops: Customer needs ETA for mitigation and asks if we can prevent future noisy neighbor effects.

julie-se: We'll propose: per-tenant packing profiles (min_batch_tokens, pack_timeout), a tenant weight in fairqueue, and autoscale sensitivity tuned to pack success rate (not just queue length). Also add an alert for "packing-timeout-rate > 1%" which would surface this earlier.

miguel.eng: Repro steps for local test (so eng can reproduce): 
1) spin up local continuous packer with min_batch_tokens=64, pack_timeout=120ms
2) send 200 qps of short requests (avg tokens ~12) from 2 tenants (A: 60% of traffic, B: 40%)
3) observe packer logs and count 429s after packing timeout

Example load command: 
```
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --script=short_prompt.lua http://dp-local:8080/v1/generate
```

and short_prompt.lua should send small prompts (~12 tokens).

alex-oncall: I'll apply the temporary fix now (per-dp min_batch_tokens=8) and monitor. Will update in 10m.

miguel.eng: After patching node-1 in dp-west-42: pack_success_rate jumped from 22% -> 78% on that node, token/sec recovered ~3x. Dashboard: queue length drained in ~2m.

sara.ops: customer confirmed error rate dropped and latency returned to normal. They're still worried about future regressions.

julie-se: Follow-ups: 
- Patch: implement per-tenant packing profile and defaults that adapt to request size distribution.
- Ops: add an alert for continuous-packer:pack-timeout-rate and pack_success_rate decay.
- SRE: add canary check in config rollout that runs short-load microbench to validate min_batch_tokens bump won't break short request tenants.

miguel.eng: Also propose adding a scheduler-tuning knob: when packer detects high fraction of tiny requests, auto-relax min_batch_tokens to X% of avg observed tokens for a grace window.

alex-oncall: Noted. For audit: config commit id that caused this was 9f2b7c (bumped to 64). Rolling back per-dp is done and I'll file a postmortem with metrics.

sara.ops: I'll reply to customer with timeline, mitigation done, and next steps. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy patch started for dp-west-42 (patch-id: patch-20251103-01)

miguel.eng: Closing thread once postmortem + follow-ups assigned.

(End of thread)
